origins: A birth condition, learning difference, or inherited trait can feel like proof that we came into the world flawed. Comparisons, medical language, and remarks from others can deepen the feeling of being a mistake.
teaches: “For You formed my inmost being; You knit me together in my mother’s womb.” God said to Jeremiah, “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.” When the disciples asked about a man born blind, Jesus said, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.” God asked Moses, “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?” You are not a mistake. God knew you, formed you, and has a purpose for you.
self_statements: Something went wrong with me from the start.
I was never meant to be.
errors: Believing I am either made perfectly or defective.
Feeling different and concluding that I was made wrong.
questions: What does God say about how I was formed?
What gifts do I have that go along with how I was made?
What purposes might God have for me?
What would I say to a baby born with my condition?
truth: God formed me and knew me before I was born. I am not a mistake. My life has purpose, and His works can be displayed in me.
hw_truths: He knew me before I was born.
God’s works can be displayed in me.
God made me as I am.
log: Each week, note one strength or purpose that is part of you.
actions: Mark each line that speaks of your making.
prayer: Creator God, You knit me together and knew me before I was born. Heal my sense of being a mistake and show me Your purpose for me. Amen.
